blocks.prompt: 5. [printed as 4.] Find the area bounded by the parabola \(y = x^{2} - 6x + 8,\ x = 2,\ x = 4\) and the \(x\)-axis.
blocks.explanation:
Ghaur kijiye: lines \(x = 2\) aur \(x = 4\) bilkul parabola ke roots hain.
Parabola upar khulta hai (seedha pyala), is liye roots ke darmiyan woh \(x\)-axis ke neeche hota hai.
Matlab integral negative aayega aur area us ka absolute value hoga (3.7.1 ka Note 1), bilkul Example 57 ki tarah.
Plan: roots aur sign check, integral, phir absolute value.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = x^{2} - 6x + 8\), \(x = 2\), \(x = 4\) aur \(x\)-axis.
Maloom karna: band area.
Tareeqa: Agar \([a, b]\) par \(f(x) \le 0\) ho to area \(= \left|\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\right|\). Wajah yeh ke axis ke neeche strips ki height \(f(x)\) negative aati hai, aur area ke liye size chahiye.

Qadam 1: Roots aur sign
\[x^{2} - 6x + 8 = (x - 2)(x - 4)\]
\(x = 3\) par: \(y = 9 - 18 + 8 = -1 < 0\).
Kyun: Factorization se roots 2 aur 4 mile, jo di gayi lines hi hain. Test point \(x = 3\) ne bata diya ke darmiyan curve neeche hai; \((3, -1)\) parabola ka vertex (sab se nicha point) bhi hai.

Qadam 2: Integrate karein
\[F(x) = \dfrac{x^{3}}{3} - 3x^{2} + 8x\]
\[F(4) = \dfrac{64}{3} - 48 + 32 = \dfrac{16}{3}\]
\[F(2) = \dfrac{8}{3} - 12 + 16 = \dfrac{20}{3}\]
\[\int_2^4 y\,dx = \dfrac{16}{3} - \dfrac{20}{3} = -\dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: Har term par power rule: \(\int x^{2} = \frac{x^{3}}{3}\), \(\int 6x = 3x^{2}\), \(\int 8 = 8x\). Phir upar wali limit minus neeche wali limit.
Dhyan dein: \(F(4)\) mein \(-48 + 32 = -16\) aur \(\frac{64}{3} - 16 = \frac{16}{3}\); fractions ko ek denominator par la kar hisaab kijiye.

Qadam 3: Area
\[A = \left|-\dfrac{4}{3}\right| = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: Minus sign sirf yeh batata hai ke region axis ke neeche hai; area hamesha positive hota hai, jaise kisi khet ka rakba kabhi minus nahi hota.

Tasdeeq:
Parabola \(y = (x - \alpha)(x - \beta)\) ke roots ke darmiyan area ka shortcut \(\frac{(\beta - \alpha)^{3}}{6}\) hai. Yahan \(\frac{2^{3}}{6} = \frac{4}{3}\). Jawab mil gaya.
